seo_meta_description: Master Exponential Functions on the Digital SAT using built-in Desmos graphing calculator hacks, syntax commands, regressions, and speed drills.
exam_weightage: Essential Digital SAT Tool (5-8 Questions per Module)

techniques.title: Exponential Regression for Data Points
techniques.description: Use the tilde (~) operator to find the base and initial value of an exponential function when given a table of values.
techniques.when_to_use: When the problem provides a table of (x, y) values and asks for the function equation.
techniques.pro_tip: Always check the 'r^2' value; if it's 1, your model is perfect.

techniques.title: Slider-Based Parameter Matching
techniques.description: Define a function with variables 'a' and 'b', then click 'add all sliders' to adjust them until the graph passes through given points.
techniques.when_to_use: When you have two points and need to find the specific exponential equation.
techniques.pro_tip: Use the 'step' feature on sliders to quickly snap to integer values.

techniques.title: Intersection of Two Functions
techniques.description: Graph both equations and click the gray dot at the intersection point to find the solution.
techniques.when_to_use: When solving for the value of x where two exponential growth/decay models meet.
techniques.pro_tip: If the intersection is off-screen, use the wrench icon to adjust the window.

techniques.title: Evaluating Functions at Specific Inputs
techniques.description: Define the function once, then type 'f(5)' to instantly evaluate the function at x=5.
techniques.when_to_use: When asked for the value of a population or amount after a specific time t.
techniques.pro_tip: Use function notation f(x) instead of y= to keep your workspace organized.

techniques.title: Vertical/Horizontal Asymptote Visualization
techniques.description: The constant 'k' represents the horizontal asymptote. Graphing it helps visualize the limit of the function.
techniques.when_to_use: When asked for the range of an exponential function or the long-term behavior.
techniques.pro_tip: Type 'y = k' as a dashed line to clearly see the boundary.

speed_walkthroughs.problem: The population of a bacteria colony doubles every 3 hours. If the initial population is 50, which function models the population $P$ after $t$ hours?
traditional_method: Step 2: Plug in a=50, b=2, d=3
desmos_hack: Step 3: Check the point (3, 100) to confirm doubling

drills.question: Which function represents the graph that passes through (0, 3) and (1, 6)?
explanation: Step 2: Check which graph passes through (0,3) and (1,6).

drills.question: If $f(x) = 100(0.5)^x$, what is the value of $f(4)$?
explanation: Step 2: Type f(4) in the next line to get the result.
